title: King & Pawn Endgames
subtitle: The square of the pawn, and escorting it home.
goals: Use the square rule to catch runners
Escort pawns with the king in front
Win races with the outside passer decoy

steps.say: In pawn endgames the king transforms: from hunted to hunter. Two skills decide almost every one: counting whether a king can CATCH a running pawn, and using your king as the escort your own pawn needs. Master these and 'equal' endgames become wins.

steps.prompt: White's a-pawn is sprinting and your king is the only defense. Can you catch it? Use the SQUARE rule!
hints: Draw a square from the pawn to its queening rank: a4–a8–e8–e4. If your king can step INSIDE it, the pawn is caught.
e4 and e5 are inside the square. Anything further right is a spectator's seat.

line.say: Inside the square! Now for every pawn step your king takes one too — mathematically guaranteed to arrive in time.
Inside the square on the diagonal — the fastest route in king geometry. The pawn will be met at the door.

rejections.say: One square outside! Count it: a5, a6, a7, a8 — your king arrives exactly one move late and the pawn queens. The square rule is unforgiving arithmetic.

steps.wrongSay: Visualize the box from a4 to e8. Your king must step INSIDE it this very move.
steps.successSay: No more move-by-move counting — one glance at the square tells you catch or no catch.

steps.prompt: Your pawn wants to promote — but pawns can't walk alone. Which piece leads the parade?
hints: Golden rule: the KING leads, the pawn follows. A pawn ahead of its escort gets blockaded and eaten.
Bring your king up in front of the pawn before pushing anything.

line.say: The escort takes the lead. The king will clear the road ahead; the pawn strolls safely behind. This order — king first — wins; the reverse draws.

rejections.say: Ke6! The black king blockades in front, your king is too far behind to help, and the pawn is frozen — then lost. Pawns ahead of their king are orphans.

steps.wrongSay: Don't touch the pawn yet — the king must get in front of it first.
steps.successSay: King endings are footraces where the king is the star. The pawn is just the trophy.

steps.prompt: Your king stands proudly ahead of its pawn — the winning setup. Now convert: escort the pawn all the way!
hints: With the king on the 6th rank in front of the pawn, this is ALWAYS winning. Advance the pawn under the king's wing.
Push e6, and when the black king blocks on e8, push e7 — he'll have to step aside, and your king shields the coronation.

line.say: The pawn reaches the seventh — protected by your king — and Black is in zugzwang: he MUST abandon the queening square.
The king takes the last guard post: e8 is secured, and nothing in the world stops e8=Q next move.

rejections.say: Drifting sideways lets the black king plant himself on e7 in front of the pawn. Your king was already perfectly placed — march the PAWN behind it.

steps.wrongSay: King on the 6th, ahead of the pawn — the position wins itself if you advance the pawn under cover.
steps.successSay: King ahead on the sixth = always winning. Burn that picture into memory — it's the destination of every winning pawn ending.

steps.prompt: The famous OUTSIDE passed pawn: your a-pawn can't queen by itself — but that was never its job. Use it as bait!
hints: Push the a-pawn: Black's king MUST chase it — it's too dangerous to ignore. Then count what your king does with the free time.
While the king trudges to the a-file, your king raids the OTHER side of the board and wins the f-pawn — and the game.

line.say: The decoy runs! Black's king has no choice but to chase...
...while your king heads the other way — toward the REAL prize.
The a-pawn will be caught — but your king has eaten the f-pawn and now escorts his own passer home, miles ahead of the returning king. The outside passer wins by dying.

rejections.say: Babysitting the a-pawn wastes its whole purpose — it's a DECOY, not a treasure. Push it and let Black's king pay the chasing fee while yours raids the kingside.

steps.wrongSay: The a-pawn is a decoy, not a queen candidate. Push it and make the enemy king pay for every step.
steps.successSay: The outside passed pawn — the endgame's most famous sacrifice. It trades its life for the whole opposite wing.
